item.title: 17-Year-Old’s Campaign Against Plastic Cutlery Prevents 8.1 Million Single-Use Utensils
item.description: Landon Hoberman, a 17-year-old from New Jersey, has made remarkable strides in reducing plastic cutlery usage in restaurants. His campaign has succeeded in keeping over 8 million utensils out of landfills, while restaurants collectively saved more than $200,000 by making cutlery optional for takeaway. This initiative showcases how small changes can lead to significant environmental impact and financial savings, presenting a scalable model for communities seeking to tackle single-use plastics.

item.title: Hello Kitty's spy drama lands in hot water: What went wrong with Sanrio in China
item.description: Sanrio has come under fire in China for its collaboration with the Japanese drama VIVANT, which many viewers found offensive. The show's depiction of a fictional Chinese intelligence agency apprehending Japanese spies has ignited fierce online backlash. In response to the criticism from the public and state media, Sanrio's Chinese branch announced it would end the partnership, highlighting the hurdles international companies endure due to ongoing Sino-Japanese tensions.
item.dc:creator: Shivanghi Payal

item.title: Meet 12-year-old Indian-American Sophia Parekh, who has given over 8,000 free books to children
item.description: Sophia Parekh, a 12-year-old from Westfield, New Jersey, has distributed more than 8,000 free books to children across the US through Sophia's Book Stand, a project she started at age seven during the Covid pandemic. She personally selects books based on children's ages and interests and also supports teachers in underserved schools. Her efforts earned her recognition as a runner-up for the 2026 Gloria Barron Prize for Young Heroes.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Quebec home built from 200,000 recycled bottles, assembled in just three days
item.description: In a remarkable development, a two-bedroom house located in Saint-Rémi-d'Amherst, Quebec, has been built using an innovative construction method known as PakVert. This technique employs panels crafted from recycled plastic bottles, resulting in a building process that took merely three days. By minimizing construction waste and cutting costs by approximately 35 percent, this initiative contributes significantly to affordable housing and environmental sustainability in Canada.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Lost Renaissance plaques found in English home sell for £100,000 after 142 years
item.description: A pair of exquisite 16th-century maiolica plaques by renowned artist Francesco Xanto Avelli recently fetched an impressive £100,000 at auction after lying unnoticed in a Dorset home for years. The family unearthed these extraordinary pieces while seeking expert advice, discovering they were part of a significant series illustrating the tale of Cyrus the Great. This auction underscores the remarkable rarity and cultural value of these Italian Renaissance treasures.

item.title: Husband’s home valuation rejected in Tennessee divorce appeal
item.description: In a contentious marital dispute, a Tennessee appeals court confirmed the trial court's assessment of a marital home valued at $160,400, awarding the wife 75% of the home's equity—approximately $47,139. The husband's higher valuation based on comparable sales was dismissed by the court. Moreover, the court invalidated the husband's artwork and tool valuations, mandating their reassessment. It also made essential amendments to the permanent parenting plan concerning visitation rights.

item.title: How two US friends turned a small haunted house into a multimillion-dollar Halloween business
item.description: Two friends, Chris Stafford and Warren Conard, opened a haunted house in a Denver shopping complex in 2002, charging $15 per ticket. What began as a side business has grown into a multimillion-dollar company with 18 seasonal Halloween attractions across the US. The company paid around 4,500 workers during the 2025 Halloween season and is now expanding into Christmas entertainment.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Arkansas took just 1.62 acres from a family trust and valued the loss at $417,825; after an 11-year fight over road access, court upholds $3 million award
item.description: A long-standing legal dispute in Arkansas involved a land acquisition that significantly impacted property access. The Arkansas Court of Appeals recently upheld a $3 million jury compensation award related to this case. The case emerged after the Arkansas State Highway Commission's project restricted access to a property owned by the William Major Lewis Trust. Evidence submitted demonstrated that the remaining property value was adversely affected by the highway work.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Georgia couple won $37 million after their 3-year-old son died during cancer treatment; judge cut it to $2 million, appeals court raises award to $3 million
item.description: A couple in Georgia has triumphed in their legal battle, securing a $3 million judgment after an appeals court re-evaluated their son's death case. This decision overturned a previous reduction of a $37 million jury award to just $2 million. Their son, who succumbed to stage-four Burkitt lymphoma, faced complications during his treatment. The court recognized the parents as distinct entities under state law, enabling them to seek higher restitution.

item.title: In 2022, AMP built its streaming base in Georgia; four years later, Kai Cenat's creator collective reportedly purchased six nearby homes and named the area 'The Hill'
item.description: Leading creators, including Kai Cenat and Fanum, have acquired six properties in Georgia, transforming them into a vibrant communal living environment for their crew and accomplices. Their earlier base in Marietta fostered content creation and gaming endeavors. With this new acquisition, the team enhances collaboration and innovation, showcasing their dedication to teamwork and growth in the digital landscape.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: Indiana woman keeps home bought with $10,000 family loan after ex-partner’s brother seeks sale
item.description: In a legal victory, Gina Behny has maintained ownership of her house after a dispute with her ex-partner's brother, Terry Curella. Purchasing the home in 1999 with help from her grandparents, Behny's extensive investments over 25 years were key. The Indiana Court of Appeals affirmed the lower court's ruling, noting Behny's substantial financial input against Curella's slight involvement, alongside an order for Curella to pay Behny for incurred losses.
